questions.q: What is a MID Server, physically?
options: A ServiceNow-hosted cloud service that runs alongside the instance
A lightweight Java application the customer installs on their own machine, inside their own network or cloud VPC
A browser extension installed on the admin's workstation
A configuration flag that enables REST Messages on an instance
questions.explain: A MID Server is a real Java application the customer downloads and installs on infrastructure they own — never something ServiceNow hosts in its own cloud.

questions.q: Why can't a ServiceNow instance simply call an internal database or legacy on-prem application directly, the way it calls a SaaS vendor's REST API?
options: Legacy applications never expose any kind of API
The instance runs in ServiceNow's own cloud, while those internal systems sit behind a corporate firewall with no public-facing endpoint to call
ServiceNow's REST Message feature doesn't support calling databases
Internal systems are always too slow to respond to an HTTP call
questions.explain: There's no reachable URL on the other end — the internal system has no public endpoint, by design, because it sits behind the customer's firewall.

questions.q: Which direction does a MID Server initiate its connection to the ServiceNow instance?
options: Inbound-only, with the instance opening a connection into the customer's network
Bidirectional, with both sides initiating connections equally
Outbound-only, from inside the customer's network out to the instance, polling for work
The MID Server never connects to the instance at all once installed
questions.explain: The MID Server always reaches outward to the instance and polls for work; the instance never initiates a connection into the customer's network.

questions.q: What specific security requirement does the outbound-only connection design satisfy?
options: The customer never has to open an inbound firewall port into their own network
The customer must open an inbound port for ServiceNow's cloud IP range
It eliminates the need for any authentication between the MID Server and the instance
It allows the firewall to be removed entirely
questions.explain: Security teams default to keeping firewalls closed to inbound traffic; because the MID Server always calls out, that posture never has to change.

questions.q: Where does the MID Server's status and version information get tracked on the ServiceNow side?
options: In the customer's firewall configuration logs
It isn't tracked anywhere — ServiceNow has no visibility into the MID Server at all
In the instance's MID Server table, which the MID Server reports back to as it polls
In a spreadsheet the admin maintains manually outside the instance
questions.explain: The MID Server table is the instance-side record of each installed MID Server's status, version, and validation state.
